exploration.title: Magnetic Fields
exploration.subject: Physics
exploration.summary: Predict, then test how reversing one complete bar changes its interaction and how two nonzero fields can cancel at one exact probe location.
exploration.question: How do two complete bar magnets set one compass direction, and when can their fields cancel?
exploration.explanation: A compass is a small magnet whose north-seeking end aligns with the local magnetic field. Outside a bar magnet, conventional field direction runs from its north pole toward its south pole. Fields from both bars combine by vector addition, so a compass responds to the local sum rather than simply choosing the nearest pole. Unlike facing poles attract and like facing poles repel. In this model, equal opposing contributions cancel at the exact midpoint between like facing poles, but each magnet still produces a field elsewhere. The bars are represented by paired softened signed sources only to approximate the exterior tabletop field; these are not isolated magnetic poles. The 0–100 field index and diagram-unit distances are normalized comparisons, not tesla, metres, force measurements or a prediction of magnet motion.

experiments.title: Reverse one magnet
experiments.instruction: Predict first. Start with N–S facing, then reverse only the right magnet to make N–N face. Hold the 2-unit gap, probe position (0, 2) and identical bars fixed.
experiments.observe: N–S facing poles attract; N–N facing poles repel. Compare the north-seeking direction and normalized field index. Explain why reversing one complete bar changes both its pole labels and its contribution to the combined field.

experiments.title: Test cancellation
experiments.instruction: Predict first. Keep N–N poles facing at gap 2. Start with the probe at (0, 0), then change only probe z to 2. Hold both magnets and probe x fixed.
experiments.observe: At the exact midpoint, two equal nonzero contributions oppose and the normalized combined index is 0, so there is no preferred direction. Away from the midpoint the combined field is nonzero. Explain why cancellation at one point does not switch off either magnet.

exploration.misconception: Field lines are a mapping tool, not material threads, flowing substance or particle paths. For a real magnet they form closed loops, including through the magnet; the displayed exterior lines and their spacing are illustrative.
